steps.body: Distributing works the same way with a **negative** multiplier — every term still gets multiplied, sign included. -3(x + 2) = -3x + (-3)(2) = -3x − 6.

widget.prompt: Cover this rectangle with tiles. One edge is −3, the other is (x + 2) — work out how many of each tile it takes, then set them.
widget.successFeedback: −3x − 6. Three copies of −(x + 2): three negative x-tiles and three negative 2s. The −3 reached every tile inside the brackets, sign and all.
widget.xFeedback: Check the x-tiles. Three copies of the group means three x-tiles, and the −3 makes every one of them negative.
widget.constFeedback: Check the units. Each of the three copies carries a 2, and the minus reaches those as well — so it is −6, not −2 and not +6.
widget.partialProductFeedback: The −3 reached the x and stopped: one copy of the 2 came out instead of three, so the mat reads −3x + 2. Look at the rectangle — every part that needs a unit tile is still uncovered.
widget.unopenedFrameFeedback: Nothing is on the mat yet. Read the rectangle: how many x-tiles fit along the −3 edge, and how many unit tiles fill what is left?

predict.prompt: Distributing −3 across (x + 2) — does the NEGATIVE reach both terms inside?

options.label: No — only the x takes the sign

predict.reveal: The −3 is one package — sign included — and distribution copies the whole package onto every term. Losing the minus on the second term is the classic slip.

explanationVariants: 2 times x is 2x, and 2 times -5 is -10.
The multiplier reaches every term, sign included.

commonBuilds.feedback: The multiplier 2 must reach the -5 too: 2 × -5 = -10, not -5.

widget.missFeedback: Multiply the outside number by BOTH terms inside — including its sign.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 2 times x is 2x, and 2 times -5 is -10.

steps.body: Check any distribution by evaluating both the original and expanded form at the same x — they must match at EVERY value, not just one.

commonErrors.feedback: Don't stop at -3×1. Finish inside the parentheses first: -3(1+2) = -3(3) = -9.

steps.body: Two negatives multiply to a positive — the same sign rule from the last course applies here too. -2(x − 6) = -2x + 12.

options.label: -2x + 12
options.feedback: Yes — -2 times x is -2x, and -2 times -6 is +12 (same signs).

options.label: -2x - 12
options.feedback: -2 times -6 is +12 (same signs multiply to positive), not -12.

options.label: 2x + 12
options.feedback: The x-term keeps the -2's sign too: -2x, not 2x.

explanationVariants: 4 times x is 4x, and 4 times -3 is -12.

commonBuilds.feedback: The multiplier 4 must reach the -3 too: 4 × -3 = -12.

widget.missFeedback: Multiply the outside number by BOTH terms inside — including its sign.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 4 times x is 4x, and 4 times -3 is -12.

commonErrors.feedback: Don't stop at 2×2. Finish inside the parentheses: 2(2-5) = 2(-3) = -6.

explanationVariants: -5 times x is -5x, and -5 times -2 is +10 (same signs).
Same signs give a positive result.

commonBuilds.feedback: -5 times -2 is +10 (same signs multiply to positive), not -10.
The x-term keeps the -5's sign too: -5x, not 5x.

widget.missFeedback: Multiply the outside number by BOTH terms inside — including its sign.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — -5 times x is -5x, and -5 times -2 is +10 (same signs).

hints: Multiply -5 by -2: same signs give a positive, so +10.

steps.body: Distributing with a negative multiplier follows the same sign rules — every term gets multiplied, sign included.
takeaways: The multiplier reaches every term inside the parentheses.
Use the sign rule: same signs positive, different signs negative.
Check by evaluating both forms at the same x-value.
